title: D-Day 81st Anniversary Protest
description:
This Friday June 6th is the 81st anniversary of D-Day. It will be a day of peaceful protest to commemorate the sacrifices of D-Day veterans, and to defend the US Constitution from threats to Democracy — the very democracy our D-Day veterans fought so hard to protect.

The protest is inspired by the “Bonus Army of 1932,” which marched on Washington in the summer of 1932 to successfully persuade politicians to re-instate promised WWI combat bonuses. Just like the Bonus Army of 1932, this Friday’s protests around the country, and on the Burnsville NC Square, will bring the threat of vanishing veterans’ rights to the forefront.

President Donald J. Trump is making quick work of erasing the history and benefits of millions of veterans. Trump’s announcement to rename “Veteran’s Day” to “Victory Day for WWI,” erases the very history of millions of veterans who served after WWI—specifically the millions who served in WWII, Korea, Vietnam, Iraq, Afghanistan, and countless other operations.

Current chaos and cuts to the Veterans Administration have already hobbled the system. Internal VA emails reveal that thousands of the 9 million veterans currently receiving benefits are already enduring gut wrenching cuts. These include loss of cancer treatments, loss of temporary housing for homeless vets, and loss of PACT Act protections to vets exposed to burn pits and other atrocities. Proposed downsizing of VA staff by 70,000 and DOGE-proposed closures of more than17 hospitals will be catastrophic.

Come join us Friday June 6th from 11:30-1:30 at the Burnsville NC Square to support veterans, the US Constitution, and the Declaration of Independence. The event will include readings of both documents, and will include “take-the-oath” ceremonies for any citizen wanting to take the oath to protect and defend the constitution. Anyone who has already taken the oath as part of their job requirement, such as civil servants, politicians, lawyers, judges, or anyone else, may come to re-commit to their oath by re-taking it.

“All US residents, including our bravest —our veterans — are entitled to the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” said Lea Charlton, a co-founder of Mountain Indivisible of WNC. “We should all be committed every day to protecting those rights.” Mountain Indivisible of WNC is sponsoring the event. It organizes pro-democracy events in Mitchell and Yancey Counties, and supports efforts in Avery County.

Our Minnetonka Wednesday Weekly Protest event is a peaceful, legal, nonviolent, family-friendly expression of first amendment rights. We will gather on the public sidewalks and grassy banks along the road margins at the intersection of Minnesota State Highway 7 and County Road 101 in Minnetonka where we will display our hand-made signs in view of evening rush hour traffic at a busy intersection. The convener is experienced in protesting at this location in all kinds of weather. The Highway 7 corridor includes communities with some of the highest voter turnout and civic engagement in the entire country. Residents here span the whole political spectrum of the United States of America, but we all agree that there are no kings in America. In between elections, we remind elected officials that no one is above the law and every elected official is accountable to the people under the Constitution. We affirm that American values of democracy, freedom, and rule of law and opposition to Trump's unaffordable policies are broadly supported in our community. 

The Wednesday 4 June 2025 event is the fifth in a planned long series of Minnetonka Wednesday Weekly Protest events that will continue indefinitely on each Wednesday afternoon through summer, autumn, winter, and into next year as needed until further notice.

description:
NO KINGS (or Oligarchs or Kleptocrats) Flag Day MARCH for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

Join us on Saturday, June 14th at 10:00 AM for the Flag Day March for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion—a bold, peaceful demonstration across the Broadway Bridge in Little Rock, Arkansas. We march to uplift the voices of the marginalized, to call for justice in our communities, and to affirm that diversity, equity, and inclusion are not optional—they are essential.

📍Meet-up spot: Margaret Clark Adventure Park (Little Rock Riverfront Park) under the Broadway Bridge

🅿️ PARKING INFORMATION:

UNDER THE BROADWAY BRIDGE- This parking location is right next to the meet-up spot and is accessible to those who have mobility needs. 

If you start in front of the Robinson Center, you will go WEST on Markham Street, cross over Broadway Street, and take the first right on Bruce Moore/Arch Street. This street dead-ends at the parking lot.

OTHER PARKING: You are also welcome to park anywhere downtown. If you park downtown near Robinson Center/The Old State House Museum/Doubletree Hotel—
Walk down Conway Street (which runs between Doubletree Hotel and Old State House Museum), over the pedestrian bridge, and that will lead you directly to our meeting spot.

🗓️ SCHEDULE:

9:30AM- Begin gathering at the above Meet-Up spot (more details, maps, and flyers to follow)

10:00AM- Walk across the Broadway Bridge, turn around at NLR Riverfront Park, walk back across the bridge.

~10:45AM- Short Rally @ The Meet-Up Spot

The short rally at the end will include speakers, music, and a united call to action.

🧳 PLEASE BRING:

👟Comfortable shoes
💦 Water!!
☀️Weather-appropriate clothing
🧴Sunscreen
🪧Protest Signs, Flags, and Umbrellas

☂️PROTEST UMBRELLAS:

Decorate an umbrella with protest messages to use as shade!

June 14th also marks Donald Trump’s birthday, a day he has chosen to celebrate with talk of military parades and authoritarian posturing. We reject fear-mongering and exclusion. Instead, we choose unity. While others parade power, we march with purpose. We show the world that our strength lies in compassion, community, and collective action.

We believe that diversity strengthens us, equity uplifts us, and inclusion unites us. Whether you’re marching for racial justice, LGBTQ+ rights, accessibility, gender equity, immigrant protections, or education equity—your voice matters here.

Let’s reclaim June 14th as a day of people power. Together, we march—for a world where everyone belongs.

description:
Please join Everyday Activists and Indivisible Shoreline WA at this event!! Saturday, June 14 is a Nationwide Day of Defiance. 

Cadet Bone Spur is spending millions on a military parade in D.C. This is the first time in U.S. history that a President has made a public spectacle to celebrate his own birthday. You know who does that? Kings.
Adding insult to injury, this comes on the back of the recent cuts to services for hundreds of millions of low-income citizens. Join us in sending the message loud and clear: We. Have. No. King.


What To Know:
This is not our usual site: it's Shoreline's Park at Town Center, often called "Sculpture Park". Completely accessible for people with mobility issues, this ten-block strip of grass has a wide, paved path, providing everything we need for this event:
- Rally: we meet at the north end of the park (Aurora Ave N & N 185th St, near the closed Bartell Drug store) for a few brief remarks and some chants to rev us up
- March: those who wish to march will be led by Everyday Activists core members proudly bearing a "No Kings" banner
- Sign-waving: those who prefer to stand or sit have lots of space to do so along the perimeter of the park itself, or lining the sidewalk on the opposite side of Aurora (the Fred Meyer side). Feel free to bring a chair.

Transportation, Parking and Bathrooms
- Transportation: We encourage participants to carpool or use public transport. There are Metro bus stops at both ends of the park (N 175th St and N 185th St). Buses also run north and south along Aurora.
- Parking: Is available on side streets between N 175th and N 185th St, but not along Aurora Ave itself. There is limited parking along Midvale Ave, which runs between the park and Shoreline City Hall. It would be nice if we could save those few spaces for people with mobility issues. Please do not park at City Hall. We have paid to use only the park; another event is taking place at City Hall. They have the use of parking there: we do not.

Security
Everyday Activists volunteers will be on hand to provide information, assistance, and basic first aid if needed. Look for the folks in the tasteful yellow safety vests. 

Volunteers
We need more volunteers. Your job will be to roam a particular segment of the park, keeping an eye out for people needing help as well as anyone causing a disruption. Note that you will not be expected to deal with disruptions yourself, but you will know who to report them to so a trained individual can respond appropriately. There will be a meeting before the event to outline your role. Please email Sandy directly (EverydayActivistsUSA@gmail.com) if you'd like to know more.
accessibility_notes: Bathrooms: There are no public bathrooms, but there are a dozen small businesses in the shopping center adjacent to the park (Starbucks, Orange Julius, etc.). Be prepared to make a small purchase in order to use the facilities.

title: NO KINGS UN-PARADE PITTSFORD, NY

location.venue: S Main St. & State St. Intersection Pittsford

description:
GRIT—Greater Rochester Integrity and Truth—is joining the national No Kings Day movement in a nationwide day of protest — and we’re taking it to the burbs. 

Rather than marching, our Un-Parade Protest will take the form of peaceful parade watching along traditional parade routes in suburbs and small towns across Monroe County. 

Sitting in protest is a poignant symbol, directly taking issue with Trump’s irresponsible use of taxpayer dollars, his defiance of the constitution, and his trampling of our rights. An Un-Parade also allows people of differing physical abilities and all ages to participate.

Details for Pittsford: 
Time: 8:30–10:30am

Address: 
Intersection of State St. (31) and Main St. We will set up our chairs (or stand) starting at the intersection and extend along State St. to Canal (Northfield Commons) and along Main St. toward Schoen Place, and possibly in other directions depending on how many 'parade watchers' show up. 

Suggested Parking: 
Pittsford public parking behind the library or behind Breathe Yoga. Carpool if you can.

Not in Pittsford? 
No worries, we are organizing in Fairport, Brighton*, Irondequoit and Henrietta…posting here soon! If you don’t see your town, and you want to help organize a No Kings Un-Parade, let us know: grit.roc@gmail.com
*The Rochester Chapter of 50501 is organizing Brighton, GRIT is a collaborator. See listing.

Want to Volunteer? 
1. We need marshals. It's easy, we train you via zoom.
2. We need point people to organize in towns not signed up yet.  
Reach out to us at grit.roc@gmail.com. Be sure to let us know what you’re interested in and what town you’re in.

GRIT is a local group that meets twice a month in person to share knowledge, foster action, and come together as a community to help each other navigate and push back against the current administration.

By registering for this event, it helps us know how many marshals and helpers we’ll need to have on site to ensure this a safe, peaceful event. And should any details change, it gives us an opportunity to keep you informed. Thank you for understanding.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Pride March
description:
For the first time, the Hudson Valley Pride March is coming to Kingston. As a diverse community of LGBTQ+ people, we know that we are stronger together. In the current political climate, we are seeing the systematic dismantling of our rights, specifically targeting our transgender siblings. We must resist tactics that seek to divide us.  We need to get in the streets, take up space, and demand justice for our communities. 

This is not a parade, this is a march. It is a crucial time for allies to join us in this fight. This is our opportunity to show Kingston and the whole Hudson Valley who we are and what we stand for.

On June 7th, join us outside the Community Center. The Hudson Valley Pride March will kick off at 12:00 from the corner of Wall and John Streets, at the Rainbow and Trans crosswalks in front of the Community Center, and will proceed down Wall Street, past our historic County Courthouse, around Old Dutch Church, past the Ulster County Government building and ending at Academy Green. Groups that would like to have a contingent in the March must complete the March registration form. If not part of another contingent, all individuals are welcome and encouraged to march with the Community Center contingent. After the march, we will be celebrating with a street festival on St. James St.

title: RESCHEDULED - Speak Your Mind - Todd Young Office Visit
description:
NOTE: We have rescheduled this event with times to visit Sen. Young's office on June 2, 3, or 4. This allows more constituents to visit with the Senator's staff and share their concerns. When you register, please choose one of the eleven (11) opportunities over these three days for your visit.

Speak your mind! It’s yet another Congressional Recess which means that Senator Todd Young is in Indiana to hear how his constituents feel about what’s happening under Donald Trump’s presidency. We don’t think he will be in his Indiana office during the recess, but we’re going to visit and see who is there to hear us.

Indivisible Central Indiana is offering sixty Hoosier constituents the chance to join in a concentrated communications effort at the Indianapolis office of Senator Todd Young on Monday June 2, Tuesday June 3, and Wednesday June 4.

Our message to Senator Young is this: Show courage, protect your Indiana constituents and defend the Constitution.

You will have the opportunity to speak to your concerns about what Senator Young should be doing to honor the oath of duty he took as a Marine and a Senator.

If you want to help deliver this message, sign up for a time to visit the Senator’s office on June 2, 3, or 4. There will be multiple shifts each day both morning and afternoon, eleven in all over the three days.

Senator Young’s conference room is small, so we're limiting each group to six of you, who will probably meet with the Senator’s staff. Please register for a time to visit and if you register, please plan to show up for your visit time.

More information will be provided after you register.
